newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST BOURSE ALMOST FLAT IN LOW DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST BOURSE ALMOST FLAT IN LOW DEMAND.

text.p: Trading on the Bucharest bourse stayed relatively flat on Thursday, despite some gains of the second-tier stocks as buyers were still reluctant to enter the market, brokers said.
Data showed second-tier listings achieved less than 10 percent of total turnover of 7.82 billion lei, nearly unchanged from 7.85 billion the previous day.
"Demand remained low today, with only few investors on the ask side," one broker said. He said local investment funds were expected to step into the market on Friday, boosting demand.

There was no visible effect on the market of the end of a month-long International Monetary Fund mission, which produced a revised state budget and government pledges to tackle inefficient industry by shutting down loss-making plants.
Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, were down by 0.49, 0.44 and 0.43 percent respectively.
In terma of average prices, 28 stocks went up and 20 slipped. Three stocks had no trades and ready-made factory Dorobantul remained suspended.
Arctic refrigerator maker continued to lead trading on the first tier. It closed at 3,600 lei, unchanged from the previous session, after falling to 3,400 lei in early trade amid selling pressure.
Low liquidity continued to affect the second-tier, with some stocks gaining in terms of average price.
